A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AV-DAR and contain readable text, equations, figures, and tables. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes Appendices A.1–A.2. The matching main sections support reliable comparison of retained content and newly supplied material.

before.justification: v1 reports original RIR prediction experiments across six RAF/HAA rooms, component ablations, and qualitative acoustic visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds runtime measurements, vision ablations, additional metric results, waveform comparisons, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The beam-tracing renderer, integrated positional encoding, multi-view feature aggregation, and position-dependent residual remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 documents their implementation and training recipe without establishing a change to the underlying method or objective.

E1.justification: Appendix A.1.6 adds a rendering-time test on the substantially larger Gibson Hennepin scene, approximately 600 square meters. The six-room RAF/HAA accuracy evaluation and training coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding RAF and HAA comparisons retain NAF++, INRAS++, AV-NeRF, AVR, and, for HAA, Diff-RIR. The added timing and waveform comparisons reuse existing baselines; ResNet18 is an internal encoder ablation.

E3.justification: The original splits, training fractions, HAA listener counts, and accuracy metrics remain unchanged. Added evaluations specify image-count and encoder controls, timing comparisons on the same GPU, an 8-second Gibson rendering test, and a diagnostic reanalysis excluding one failed-speaker recording.

E4.justification: v2 adds vision-count and encoder ablations, waveform fidelity comparisons, a failed-recording analysis explaining an anomalous scaling trend, and direct-sound/early-echo failure cases. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence. Table 8 repeats the existing Table 3 ablation rather than introducing another experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The appendix continues the existing practice of reporting point results.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 remain unchanged, but v2 adds HAA EDT results, RAF metric curves, vision-ablation scores, waveform examples, and computational measurements. Table 5 reports inference times of 66 ms for AV-DAR, 376 ms for DiffRIR, and 100 ms for AVR. New Table 6 gives INRAS++ Dampened Room T60 as 382.9%, conflicting with 187.1% in retained Table 2.

T1.justification: Appendices A.1.1–A.1.2 add beam-hit and time-of-arrival expressions and a derivation of the local Gaussian covariance used for beam footprints. These supply supporting mathematical details; the main formulation and assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scientific claims, including differentiable beam tracing, material-aware visual guidance, and sparse-measurement performance. The comparison against models trained with ten times more data and the 16.6%–50.9% gain range are unchanged.

C2.justification: The appendix substantially expands interpretation and limitations: visual features are interpreted as primarily helping early reflections and requiring sufficient views; aggregate metrics can miss waveform distortion; nearby source–listener pairs challenge first-arrival prediction. It also attributes an anomalous training-scale trend to a failed-speaker recording.

D1.justification: v1 defers important implementation and training details to supplementary material absent from that PDF. v2 supplies tracing pseudocode, basis-point sampling, frequency sampling, optimizer settings, batch size, progressive reflection depth, training/inference beam counts, hardware, model sizes, and timings. It also adds a project-page link, without establishing the linked resources' availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for spherical sampling, ResNet, Hearing Anywhere in Any Environment, Gibson, and Open3D. The main relationship to learning-based and physics-based prior work remains unchanged; publication updates to existing references do not constitute new positioning.

P1.justification: The main sections retain their order and largely identical prose, with limited wording and typo corrections. Additional explanations are organized into Method Details and Additional Results appendices, rather than an extensive rewrite of the main narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn to clarify rendering operations, aggregation, and gradient flow. The appendix adds geometric diagrams, waveform panels, failure visualizations, Algorithm 1, and timing, full-metric, and vision-ablation tables. Table 8 redisplays Table 3, while Figure 5 receives smaller formatting changes.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves substantial documentation and evidential gaps in the supplied v1: previously deferred renderer/training details become inspectable, measured timings support the central efficiency claim, and vision ablations and failure cases clarify effectiveness and limitations. These gains outweigh localized weaknesses, notably the conflicting INRAS++ T60 entry in Tables 2 and 6 and the inconsistent percentage identifying the failed-recording subset.
